answerCheck.reason: The actual SVG has the stated pentagon ordering A, B, C, D, E, with AB the lower-left cut of the rectangle. For P=(x, y), the dot product (A-P)dot(B-P)=x(x-4)+y(y-2) is negative exactly when(x-2)^2+(y-1)^2<5. Thus the obtuse locus is the interior of the circle with diameter AB, center(2, 1), radius sqrt(5). There is also a purely angle-based locus argument: the diameter theorem gives a right angle at each other circle point Q. If angle BAP>=90 degrees, angle APB cannot be obtuse. Otherwise ray AP meets the circle again at Q. If P lies before Q, angle APB is the exterior angle of PBQ and exceeds the right angle at Q;if P is beyond Q, triangle PQB has its right angle at Q and angle APB is acute. This proves the same inside-circle criterion without dot products. The pentagon is the rectangle 0<=x<=2 pi+1, 0<=y<=4 cut by x+2 y>=4. The diameter AB lies on the cut line, and the circle is centered on that line, so the favorable part is its upper/right semicircle. This semicircle really fits: if x<=0 and x+2 y>=4, then y>=2-x/2 and squared center distance is at least(x-2)^2+(1-x/2)^2=5-5 x+5 x^2/4>=5;similarly y<=0 would give x>=4-2 y and squared distance at least 5(1-y)^2>=5. Its remaining extents satisfy y<=1+sqrt(5)<4 and x<=2+sqrt(5)<5<2 pi+1. Hence no additional clipping occurs. Favorable area is 5 pi/2. The pentagon area is 4*(2 pi+1)-(1/2)*4*2=8 pi, so the ratio is 5/16. Boundaries have area zero.

Cone unfolding gives a sector of angle pi because the outer circular rim has circumference12*pi; diametrically opposite generators therefore differ by pi/2 in the developed angle. The straight developed chord enters the removed radius-6 disk and is inadmissible. Here is a global lower bound without assuming a new shortest-path theorem. Any continuous surface path lifts to the annular cone development with endpoint angular difference pi/2+k*pi for an integer k; after reflection its absolute angular difference is at least pi/2. It must cross the ray at angle pi/3 from A=(12,0). At a first such point P=(r/2,sqrt(3)*r/2), r>=6, the coordinate-distance formula gives AP^2=(r-6)^2+108>=108. Thus the path before P has length at least6*sqrt(3). The remaining path has net angular travel at least pi/6 and stays outside the radius-6 disk. Radial projection to that circle cannot increase length: for unit vectors u,v and r,s>=6, the squared distance identity |r*u-s*v|^2=(r-s)^2+r*s*|u-v|^2>=36*|u-v|^2 proves contraction for every chord. Apply it to every ordered path partition and take the supremum defining curve length; the projected path must cover circular angular travel at least pi/6, of length at least pi by the arc formula. Hence every path has length at least6*sqrt(3)+pi, including paths that wind or cross a development seam. Attainment is a tangent segment from A to the inner circle at angle pi/3, length 6*sqrt(3), followed by the inner-rim arc of angle pi/6, length pi. It stays within the annulus. Therefore the shortest length is 6*sqrt(3)+pi, E.
